name: SAR Filing by MLRO
description: The MLRO (PER-052) receives a trigger — either an automated system event (SanctionsHitDetected, FraudScoreCompleted) or a manual internal disclosure from staff — investigates the suspicious activity, makes a documented SAR/no-SAR decision, prepares and files a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with the NCA UKFIU via SAR Online within 5 business days of forming a suspicion. The customer is never notified at any stage (POCA 2002 s333A tipping-off prohibition). Post-filing, the MLRO manages the NCA consent regime where applicable and coordinates account restriction with Retail Banking.

sections: s332 — tipping off in regulated sector
s333A — tipping-off prohibition for nominated officers
regulatory_basis.obligation: MLRO must file a SAR if they know, suspect, or have reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering. Failure to file is a criminal offence carrying up to 5 years imprisonment.

sections: s19 — failure to disclose: regulated sector
regulatory_basis.obligation: Extends SAR obligation to suspected terrorist financing. Same tipping-off prohibition applies.

regulatory_basis.legislation: Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (MLR 2017)
sections: Regulation 40 — record-keeping (minimum 5 years, extended to 7 years by bank policy)
regulatory_basis.obligation: Bank must appoint an MLRO as nominated officer. All SAR-related records must be retained. SAR quality must be adequate for NCA intelligence purposes.

cross_capability_interactions.purpose: SVC-001 consumes SARFiled to apply account restrictions and enhanced monitoring flags to the customer's accounts where the MLRO determines restrictions are required.

tipping_off_prohibition.enforcement: The customer (PER-001) must receive no communication, notification, or indication that a SAR has been filed or is under consideration at any stage of this journey. All system notifications, UI messages, and staff communications must be reviewed for tipping-off risk before despatch.
system_controls: No customer-facing notifications triggered by SAR events
SAR workflow UI is accessible only to PER-052 and PER-053 (Deputy MLRO) — role-gated at IAM level
SARFiled event payload does not contain the word 'SAR' in any field surfaced to customer-facing services
Account restriction notices shown to the customer use generic 'account under review' language only
Audit access log for SAR records is separate from general compliance case management access

phases.name: Suspicion Trigger
phases.description: A suspicion is raised either by an automated system event or by a member of staff submitting an internal suspicious activity disclosure to the MLRO. The trigger is logged and a SARInvestigationRecord is created.

trigger_types.description: System event published by SVC-014 or fraud detection capability triggers automatic creation of a SARInvestigationRecord in SVC-014 with trigger_type = automated_event.
A member of staff submits an internal suspicious activity report to the MLRO via the MLRO case management interface. MLRO creates SARInvestigationRecord with trigger_type = staff_disclosure.
MLRO proactively opens an investigation based on transaction monitoring alerts, periodic KYC review findings, or intelligence received from NCA/law enforcement.

actions: System or staff creates trigger entry
SVC-014 creates SARInvestigationRecord (status = open)
SVC-014 publishes SARInvestigationOpened (EVT-014)
SVC-103 (Audit & Logging) records trigger event immutably
MLRO is notified via secure internal channel (not email)

phases.name: MLRO Investigation
phases.description: MLRO reviews all available evidence: customer identity data, KYC assessment, transaction history, adverse media, prior SARs, and any staff disclosure details. MLRO documents their review findings in the SARInvestigationRecord. This phase may span multiple working days but must conclude before the 5-business-day filing window closes.
actions: MLRO accesses SARInvestigationRecord via secure case management interface
MLRO reviews Customer record (ENT-001) — identity, addresses, nationality, risk flags
MLRO reviews KycAssessment (ENT-003) — risk score, PEP/sanctions screening results, EDD history
MLRO reviews transaction history — via SVC-001 read API (account activity for relevant period)
MLRO reviews any prior SARs filed for this customer (SVC-014 SAR records)
MLRO documents investigation findings in SARInvestigationRecord.evidence_items
MLRO records timeline entries as investigation progresses
phases.sla_note: Investigation must be completed in time to allow SAR preparation and filing within 5 business days of the decision to file (GOV-005-R01). Best practice: investigation target completion within 3 business days of trigger to allow 2 days for preparation.

phases.name: SAR Decision
phases.description: MLRO makes and documents their formal decision: file a SAR, file a defensive SAR, or dismiss. Decision and rationale are permanently recorded. SARDecisionMade event is published.

decision_outcomes.description: MLRO forms a suspicion on the balance of probabilities. A SAR must be filed. SuspiciousActivityReport entity is created with status = draft.
Suspicion level is low but MLRO files for protection (low-suspicion defensive filing). Entity created, notes reflect defensive rationale. Proceeds to SAR-PH-004.
MLRO is satisfied there is no money laundering or terrorist financing. Investigation is closed with documented rationale. No SAR is filed. SARInvestigationRecord.status = dismissed.

actions: MLRO documents decision rationale in SARInvestigationRecord.mlro_decision_rationale
If file or file_defensive: SVC-014 creates SuspiciousActivityReport (ENT-008) with status = draft
SVC-014 publishes SARDecisionMade (EVT-015)
SVC-103 records decision immutably with MLRO identity and timestamp

phases.name: SAR Preparation
phases.description: MLRO completes the NCA SAR Online submission form. All required fields are populated: subject details (anonymised references, not full PII in the draft), grounds of suspicion, relevant dates, transaction details, and typology indicators. MLRO reviews the draft for completeness and accuracy.
nca_form_sections: Grounds for suspicion — free text, must be specific and intelligence-bearing
Value of suspicion (estimated monetary value where quantifiable)
Bank account and sort code details
Consent request — tick box if MLRO seeks consent to proceed with a transaction
actions: MLRO opens SAR draft in SVC-014 case management (SuspiciousActivityReport status = draft)
MLRO populates all SAR fields drawing from SARInvestigationRecord evidence
System validates required fields (nca_reference will be populated post-submission)
MLRO reviews for tipping-off risk — no customer-facing language that could constitute disclosure
MLRO marks SAR as ready_for_submission
data_entities_updated: ENT-008 (SuspiciousActivityReport — all investigation and form fields)
phases.tipping_off_check: MLRO must confirm review of tipping-off risk before the submission control is enabled

phases.name: SAR Submission
phases.description: MLRO submits the SAR to the NCA UKFIU via SAR Online (SVC-014 calls NCA SAR Online API or MLRO submits via web portal). NCA acknowledges receipt and issues an NCA reference number. SARFiled event is published.
phases.submission_channel: NCA SAR Online (https://www.sars.ncsc.police.uk/) — web portal submission or API integration where available
actions: MLRO triggers submission action in SVC-014
SVC-014 submits SAR to NCA SAR Online
NCA acknowledges receipt; SVC-014 records NCA reference number in SuspiciousActivityReport.nca_reference
SuspiciousActivityReport.status transitions to filed
SuspiciousActivityReport.filed_date recorded (ISO 8601 UTC)
SVC-014 publishes SARFiled (EVT-016)
SVC-103 records submission immutably
SLA compliance check: filed_date must be within 5 business days of mlro_decision_date
phases.sla: 5 business days from MLRO decision date to filed_date (GOV-005-R01 / POCA 2002 s338)

phases.name: Post-Filing Actions
phases.description: After filing, the MLRO monitors the NCA consent regime (where applicable), coordinates account restrictions with Retail Banking, and closes the investigation record. If NCA refuses consent or imposes a moratorium, transactions are held. If consent is granted or the 7-day moratorium expires without NCA response, normal account operations resume (subject to ongoing monitoring).

consent_regime.description: If the MLRO filed a SAR seeking consent to proceed with a specific transaction (a 'consent SAR'), the bank must await NCA response before processing that transaction. NCA has 7 calendar days from receipt to refuse consent; if no response within 7 days, the bank may proceed. NCA may issue a moratorium notice extending the hold for up to 31 days (plus 31-day renewals).

actions: If consent SAR: SVC-014 publishes SARConsentRequested (EVT-017); SVC-001 places transaction on hold
MLRO monitors NCA response via SAR Online
On NCA consent grant or moratorium expiry: SVC-014 updates SuspiciousActivityReport.consent_status = granted/expired; publishes SARConsentGranted (EVT-018)
If account restrictions required: SARFiled event triggers SVC-001 to apply enhanced monitoring flag
SVC-001 publishes AccountRestrictionApplied (EVT-019)
MLRO closes SARInvestigationRecord (status = closed)
Annual MLRO report data aggregation: SAR count, typologies, consent SAR outcomes

happy_path.description: SAR filed within 5 business days of MLRO decision. No consent regime required. Account restrictions applied as needed.

alternative_paths.name: Defensive SAR
alternative_paths.description: MLRO's suspicion level is low but the MLRO files for protection. The SAR is labelled defensive in the grounds of suspicion narrative. All other steps identical to happy path.

exception_paths.name: No SAR Filed — Dismissal
exception_paths.description: MLRO is satisfied that no money laundering is occurring after investigation. SAR is dismissed with documented rationale. SARInvestigationRecord.status = dismissed.
exception_paths.outcome: SARInvestigationRecord closed. No SuspiciousActivityReport entity created.

exception_paths.name: NCA Consent Hold — Transaction Moratorium
exception_paths.description: MLRO files a consent SAR (seeking NCA permission before processing a transaction). NCA refuses consent or issues a moratorium. Transaction is held for up to 31+31 days. MLRO must not tip off the customer about the reason for the hold.
exception_paths.outcome: Transaction held until NCA consent granted, moratorium expires, or NCA extends moratorium. Customer informed only of generic account hold — no SAR reference.

exception_paths.name: Tipping-Off Incident
exception_paths.description: A member of staff inadvertently discloses to the customer that a SAR has been filed or is under consideration. This is a criminal offence under POCA 2002 s333A. Immediate escalation to MLRO and Legal. Incident is reported to the FCA under SYSC breach reporting obligations.
exception_paths.outcome: Incident investigation opened. Staff member suspended pending investigation. FCA notified. NCA potentially notified of compromise. Criminal liability assessment by Legal.

exception_paths.name: SLA Breach — 5 Business Day Window Missed
exception_paths.description: SAR is not filed within 5 business days of the MLRO forming a suspicion. This is a criminal offence under POCA 2002 s331. Immediate escalation to Board Risk Committee and Legal. Voluntary disclosure to NCA and FCA.
exception_paths.outcome: MLRO makes voluntary disclosure to NCA. Legal assesses criminal liability. FCA notified under SYSC breach reporting. Root cause analysis and remediation plan. Board report.

key_regulatory_constraints: POCA 2002 s330/s331: Criminal offence to fail to disclose suspected money laundering. Up to 5 years imprisonment.
POCA 2002 s333A: Tipping-off is a criminal offence. Customer must never be told a SAR has been filed.
MLR 2017 Regulation 40: SAR records must be retained for minimum 5 years (bank policy extends to 7 years WORM).
GOV-005-R01: SAR must be filed within 5 business days of MLRO forming a suspicion.
NCA UKFIU guidance: SAR quality (specificity of grounds, intelligence value) is under active NCA scrutiny — generic SARs risk supervisory criticism.
SM&CR: MLRO (SMF17) holds personal accountability for SAR programme quality. Non-compliance may result in FCA prohibition.
